## Mobile Game - Queue Up?
The QueueUp game is designed for casual non-gamers, something you can do while you have to wait in line. This application is all about the meta of the queue up process itself - how much time you spend on waiting for something and what you could have done instead. The game is available on iOS and Android.

## Quiz Show Game - QUEUE UP
QUEUE UP is a fast, frenetic, energetic take on a quiz show where 3 teams of 4 players compete to win by queuing behind the correct answer. In this fast-paced trivia gameshow, team members don't have to queue behind their team member if they assume they cannot give the right answer - they can jump to another line and still earn points.

## Puzzle Game - Queue Up!
Queue Up! is a short puzzle game where you must set up a store layout so that your customers leave as quickly as possible.

## Board Game - Jump the Queue
Jump the Queue is a game in which each player attempts to move five different vehicles through a queue of traffic.

There are multiple games with queue-related themes, each offering different gameplay experiences!

Here's what I found about the Q-UP game:

Q-UP is a pseudo-multiplayer incremental game where the goal is to maximize the gain of a resource called Q by creating an optimized build of skills and items. It's described as the coin flipping eSport, combining one part clicker, one part multiplayer strategy game, one part demented capitalism simulator, and 100% completely random gameplay.

It is a spiritual sequel to Universal Paperclips, where the number you are making go up is your rating in the semi-fictional game at the heart of the game. It starts out as a simple clicker and then has a bunch of twists and turns, eventually turning into something that should appeal to fans of Zachtronics-style engine-building puzzle games, visual novels about quantum mechanics, and ambient jungle.

Every single round of Q-UP is determined by the result of a coin flip, so every single round is completely fair. The game's humor is largely aimed at the esports and games industries, sending up their aesthetics and self-importance and desperate desire to force "innovation" where none exists.

The game is available on Steam and has received largely positive reviews overall, with 94% of 1,119 user reviews being positive.

content.text:
Got it — **Q-UP**, Frank Lantz's game. That's not from my training knowledge; here's what I just pulled up:

It's the spiritual sequel to **Universal Paperclips** — an incremental/clicker where the number going up is your *rating* in a fictional esport. The conceit: every round of the in-game esport is decided by a coin flip, so it's perfectly fair and perfectly meaningless. You build an optimized loadout of skills and items to farm a resource called Q.

Structurally it opens as a simple clicker and then keeps mutating — reviewers describe the late game as landing somewhere between Zachtronics-style engine-building, a visual novel about quantum mechanics, and ambient jungle. The satire is aimed squarely at the esports and games industries: the aesthetics, the self-importance, the compulsion to manufacture "innovation."

Released late 2025, on Steam with a demo, ~94% positive across ~1,100 reviews.

Caveat: everything above is from search results, not firsthand — I can't vouch for how the mid/late game actually plays. If you want, I can dig into the wiki for specifics (build theory, the phase transitions, endgame) or find writeups on the design.
